cards: How are protozoa grouped?
By motility: ameboid, ciliated, flagellated and apicomplexa
Which protozoan group lacks locomotor organelles in the trophozoite?
The apicomplexans, also called sporozoans
Which drawback do antiprotozoan drugs share as a group?
Toxicity problems and severe side effects
What does the name histolytica mean?
Tissue lysis: histo, tissue, and lytica, lysis
How do people acquire Entamoeba histolytica?
Swallowing its cysts by the fecal-oral route
Which organ does extraintestinal amebiasis invade most often?
The liver, forming abscesses: amebic hepatitis
What is the best prevention for amebiasis?
Water treatment; a vaccine is still under development
How does Naegleria fowleri get into the body?
Nasal contact with fresh water, as in diving or waterskiing
Which path does Naegleria take to the brain?
Through the nasal mucosa, then along the olfactory nerve
Which disease does Naegleria fowleri cause?
Primary amebic meningoencephalitis, fatal within days
Which Acanthamoeba infection affects contact lens wearers?
Amebic keratitis: eye pain, redness and irritation
How does Acanthamoeba enter to cause granulomatous amebic encephalitis?
Through a break in the skin or the nasal passages
Which protozoan in this lecture is a ciliate?
Balantidium coli, from the intestines of pigs and cattle
Which stage does Trichomonas lack?
The cyst: it exists only as a trophozoite
Which curable sexually transmitted disease is most common in young women?
Trichomoniasis, caused by Trichomonas vaginalis
What discharge does trichomoniasis cause in women?
A foul-smelling, green-to-yellow discharge
How is trichomoniasis diagnosed?
Microscopic analysis of a vaginal smear
What shape is the Giardia trophozoite?
Symmetrical heart shape with a ventral suction cup
Which group of people commonly gets giardiasis?
Campers, who swallow cysts in water and food
Why is microscopic diagnosis of Giardia difficult?
The organism is shed in feces only intermittently
What kills Giardia in water?
Boiling, ozone and iodine kill the agent
How are the hemoflagellates spread?
By blood-sucking insects that serve as intermediate hosts
What does a trypanosome look like on a blood smear?
Spindle-shaped, wavy flagellates swimming between red blood cells
Which vector spreads Trypanosoma brucei?
The tsetse fly, with mammals as reservoirs
What forms where the tsetse fly bites?
A primary chancre in the inoculated skin
How does Trypanosoma brucei evade the immune response?
Antigenic variation among many different antigens
Which vector spreads Trypanosoma cruzi?
The reduviid, or kissing, bug
How does Trypanosoma cruzi enter through the skin?
Bug feces are inoculated into a cutaneous portal
Why is Chagas disease a growing concern in the United States?
Its vector is migrating into the Southern United States
What is Romaña's sign?
A chagoma: eyelid swelling with conjunctivitis in Chagas disease
Which organs harbor masses of Trypanosoma cruzi?
Heart muscle and the large intestine
What is the best way to control the hemoflagellate diseases?
Vector control: eliminate the tsetse fly and control the reduviid bug
When must African sleeping sickness be treated?
Early, before neurological involvement begins
Which vector spreads Leishmania?
The female sand fly, which needs a blood meal
What is the Baghdad boil?
Cutaneous leishmaniasis: a localized ulcerated sore
What is espundia?
Chronic leishmaniasis of the skin and mucous membranes of the head
Which form of leishmaniasis is the most severe?
Kala azar, fatal if untreated
What is the primary vector of malaria?
The female Anopheles mosquito
What do merozoites become inside red blood cells?
Circular ring trophozoites that multiply until the cell bursts
Where does the sexual phase of Plasmodium take place?
Inside the female Anopheles mosquito
What causes malaria's regular chills-fever-sweating episodes?
Red blood cells rupturing, at intervals set by the species
Which Plasmodium species is the most malignant?
Plasmodium falciparum, with the highest death rate in children
Which inherited trait gives natural resistance to malaria?
The sickle cell trait
Which animal is the definitive host of Toxoplasma gondii?
The cat, which sheds oocysts in its feces
How do people acquire Toxoplasma gondii?
Eating raw meat or anything contaminated by cat feces
What can congenital toxoplasmosis cause in the newborn?
Hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis
Who develops toxoplasma encephalitis?
Immunocompromised people, such as those with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
How do humans acquire Sarcocystis?
Eating undercooked beef or pork
Why does Cryptosporidium spread in swimming pools?
It tolerates chlorine; only filtration removes it
Who suffers chronic persistent diarrhea from Cryptosporidium?
People with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and other immunocompromised patients
Whom does Isospora belli mainly affect?
Immunocompromised hosts; in others it is usually asymptomatic
How is Cyclospora cayetanensis transmitted?
Oral-fecal, through fresh produce and water
Which stain shows Cyclospora in a fecal smear?
An acid-fast stain of the fecal smear
Which tick carries Babesia microti?
The blacklegged deer tick
What does Babesia do to red blood cells?
Attacks them, which can cause hemolytic anemia
What occurs in a helminth's definitive host?
The worm reaches adulthood and mates
What occurs in a helminth's intermediate host?
The larvae develop there
What is a transport, or paratenic, host?
A host in which the parasite does not develop
Which white blood cells defend against worms?
Eosinophils are the defense against worms
How does helminth Cycle A begin?
Swallowing a mature egg in contaminated food or water
How does helminth Cycle B begin?
Infective larvae in soil penetrate the skin
How does helminth Cycle C begin?
Eating an encysted worm in undercooked meat
What defines helminth Cycle D?
An intermediate host, such as a snail or biting insect
Which roundworm's lung migration causes eosinophilic pneumonitis?
Ascaris lumbricoides, the large intestinal roundworm
What can heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infestation cause?
Dysentery and rectal prolapse, which can be fatal in children
What is the most common worm disease of children in temperate zones?
Enterobiasis: pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis
Which test diagnoses pinworm?
The tape test (a Scotch tape test)
How do Necator americanus (hookworm) larvae enter the body?
Filariform larvae burrow into the skin of bare feet
Which worm can reinfect the same host without leaving the body?
Strongyloides stercoralis, the threadworm
How do people acquire Trichinella spiralis?
Eating undercooked pork or bear meat
Which nematode causes eosinophilic meningitis?
Angiostrongylus cantonensis, the rat lungworm
What does the lumbar puncture show in rat lungworm meningitis?
Elevated eosinophils instead of neutrophils
Which vector spreads Wuchereria bancrofti?
Mosquitoes, which deposit larvae that enter the lymphatics
What does chronic Wuchereria bancrofti infection cause?
Lymphatic blockage and elephantiasis of the extremities
Which vector spreads Onchocerca volvulus?
Biting black flies, the intermediate host
What actually damages the eye in river blindness?
Inflammation against antigens of endosymbiotic Wolbachia bacteria
Which worm migrates under the skin and may enter the eye?
Loa loa, the African eye worm
How do humans acquire Toxocara canis or Toxocara cati?
Swallowing infective eggs from dog or cat feces
What is the intermediate host of Schistosoma?
A freshwater snail, which releases the cercaria
How does the Schistosoma cercaria enter humans?
It penetrates the skin in water where the snail lives
How do people acquire Opisthorchis sinensis, the Chinese liver fluke?
Eating inadequately cooked freshwater fish
How do people acquire Fasciola hepatica?
Eating raw aquatic plants
How do people acquire the lung fluke Paragonimus westermani?
Eating undercooked crustaceans such as crabs
How do people acquire Taenia saginata, the beef tapeworm?
Eating raw beef in which the larvae have encysted
What causes cysticercosis?
Swallowing embryonated eggs of Taenia solium
Where are cysticercosis cysts most damaging?
Heart muscle, eye and brain
How do people typically acquire Echinococcus?
Handling dogs that carry the infection
What does cystic echinococcosis (hydatid disease) produce?
Slowly enlarging cysts in the liver and lungs
What makes an arthropod a biological vector?
It transmits microbes in the process of feeding
Which ticks transmit relapsing fever?
Soft, or argasid, ticks with flexible bodies
